idiom_name: one request handler per page bound to its URL
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: bind each logical page or action to exactly one handler and let the container or route table select it by URL. The handler parses and validates the request, calls domain logic, then selects a view or writes the response, keeping the domain code HTTP-ignorant. Because the classic weakness is duplication, factor behaviour used by several pages into helpers, filters or a thin base — and when that shared surface starts to dominate, stop and introduce a Front Controller with an explicit dispatcher instead of growing a base controller. The per-page controller is still the right call when pages are genuinely independent and the shared surface is small.
pitfalls: Copying the previous page controller as a template, including its checks — the duplicated authorisation and error handling then drift page by page.
Letting the controller grow into model and view: SQL, business rules and HTML in the handler make it untestable and unfixable in one place.
Assuming a shared check exists elsewhere: every new page needs its own explicit validation and authorisation, because nothing intercepts requests centrally.
